States the languages are known only from South Cushitic loanwords in Dawida and Saghala plus oral tradition; cites Ehret & Nurse 1981, Nurse's paper in Bechhaus-Gerst & Serzisko (eds.) 1988 Cushitic-Omotic pp. 95, 99, Ehret 2010 pp. 203-204, Nurse & Hinnebusch 1993 p. 333, Merritt 1975 (history PhD).

sources.citation: Mulder, Sophie. 2021. The Taita Cushites revisited. BA thesis (Descriptive Linguistics), Leiden University (supervisor M. Mous). 68 pp. https://hdl.handle.net/1887/3606925
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The thesis re-examines 41 putative Southern Cushitic loanwords in Saghala/Dawida and Ehret & Nurse's segmental 'sound laws' (ch. 4-5, appendices); no section on phonology, tone, accent or stress of Taita Cushitic. The only prosodic remark is 'loss of final high tone' inside a quoted Iraqw/West-Rift reconstruction (PDF p. 45 = printed p. 44, Appendix 4).
